title: CertPool has no upper bound on pool size
description:
CertPool (pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs) accepts an unbounded number of certificates via add() and FromIterator/Extend. The DFS path builder operates on this pool with a node-visit budget (DEFAULT_DFS_BUDGET = 10,000) that bounds CPU, but the memory consumed by the pool itself has no cap. An adversarial input (e.g., a CMS SignedData.certificates bag containing millions of valid Certificate values) can force unbounded heap allocation before the path builder ever runs.

What goes wrong (availability): Memory exhaustion / OOM before the DFS budget check is reached. The budget guards CPU time, not memory.

Locations:
- /home/mark/PROJECT/PKIX/pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs lines 90-131 (CertPool::add, FromIterator, Extend)
- /home/mark/PROJECT/PKIX/pkix-chain/src/lib.rs line 603 (supplied_chain.iter().cloned().collect() into CertPool in build_with_aia)

Suggested fix: Add an optional max_certs field to PathBuilderConfig (default: something generous like 1000). CertPool::add / Extend / FromIterator could enforce a cap, or the builder functions could check pool.len() against config before proceeding. This is defense-in-depth -- callers controlling their own inputs are unaffected, but callers processing untrusted CMS bags get a bound.

Note: the DFS budget already mitigates the CPU side of adversarial pools. This finding is specifically about the memory side.
